item.title: No new Iran negotiations planned despite Trump comments, U.S. officials say
item.description: President Trump, who called Tehran "unbelievably duplicitous," said the talks are the "last chance" for Iran to forge a deal and avoid an escalation.

item.title: Zac Brown Band surprises 37,000 Fenway Park concert fans with free cruises
item.description: Zac Brown Band celebrated their 15th straight sold-out concert at Fenway Park in Boston by giving everyone a free vacation on a cruise ship.

item.title: Trump administration finalizes AI framework, official says
item.description: The order asks AI companies to share previews of powerful new models with the government before they are released to the public.

item.title: Trump says oil companies should cut gas prices after making "too much money"
item.description: President Trump said U.S. oil companies made "too much money" from high oil prices. "I'm not happy about it," he added.

item.title: Could DOJ revive the "anti-weaponization" fund even after Blanche rescinded it?
item.description: GOP Sens. John Cornyn and Thom Tillis formally announced their support for Todd Blanche as attorney general on Monday. This comes after an agreement was reached to end the controversial "anti-weaponization" fund. Rupa Bhattacharyya, legal director at the Institute for Constitutional Advocacy and Protection, joins with analysis.

item.title: Lindsay Clancy's diary excerpts read at trial: "I feel like I'm drowning"
item.description: The Lindsay Clancy trial​ resumed with excerpts from her diary and testimony from doctors who treated Clancy and her children on the night of the murders.

item.title: Martha Stewart | 60 Minutes Archive
item.description: 60 Minutes interviewed media mogul Martha Stewart several times over the years. In 1995, Morley Safer asked about the difference between Martha Stewart the brand and Martha Stewart the person. Stewart replied, "Well, there's not really much of a difference. I am Martha Stewart and my business has become also Martha Stewart. That's the complicated thing for the people who work with me." Today, the American businesswoman turns 85.

item.title: Michigan health officials report 2 deaths among cyclosporiasis cases
item.description: Two Michigan residents who had "significant underlying health conditions" have died after contracting cyclosporiasis, the Michigan Department of Health and Human Services said.

item.title: Trump says Jeanine Pirro "choked" in dropping Reflecting Pool case
item.description: "She folded like an umbrella," President Trump said of Jeanine Pirro, U.S. Attorney for the District of Columbia.

item.title: Cornyn, Tillis back Blanche for attorney general after deal on DOJ fund
item.description: GOP Sens. John Cornyn of Texas and Thom Tillis of North Carolina formally announced their support on Monday for Todd Blanche's nomination for attorney general.

item.title: Spain to put containment fence around Ceuta after deadly border rush from Morocco
item.description: Spain says it will build a 1,600-foot containment fence around its enclave of Ceuta after thousands of migrants rushed its border with Morocco last week. CBS News' Aidan Stretch reports.

item.title: Abdul El-Sayed on socialist labels, who he thinks belongs in the Democratic Party
item.description: Democratic Senate candidate Dr. Abdul El-Sayed speaks with CBS News' Ed O'Keefe about his constituency and what he would like the Democratic Party to look like as his primary run against Rep. Haley Stevens reaches its final stretch.

item.title: What to know about Taylor Farms amid the cyclospora outbreak
item.description: The nation's largest recent cyclospora outbreak has put one of America's biggest produce suppliers under renewed scrutiny.

item.title: Takeaways after Trump takes questions on Iran, Reflecting Pool in Oval Office
item.description: President Trump took reporter questions on the Iran war, the renovation of the reflecting pool in Washington, D.C., and more on Monday. CBS News' Lindsey Reiser and Natalie Brand share their biggest takeaways.

item.title: House Ethics recommends censure for GOP lawmaker in sexual harassment probe
item.description: The House Ethics Committee released a report detailing the findings of an investigation into GOP Rep. Chuck Edwards, concluding that there is "substantial reason to believe" he violated House rules.

item.title: Watch: Trump takes questions on Iran war, Reflecting Pool, immigration, more
item.description: President Trump took reporter questions on topics ranging from the war with Iran to immigration and energy prices in the Oval Office on Monday. Following his remarks, CBS News' Natalie Brand added further context.

item.title: What to watch for in SpaceX's first public earnings report this week
item.description: SpaceX will release its first earnings report as a public company on Tuesday in a key test for the company's stuttering stock price.

item.title: Acting attorney general issues order rescinding "anti-weaponization" fund
item.description: The order came after Republican Senators Thom Tillis and John Cornyn threatened to block Blanche's confirmation for Attorney General if the fund was not rescinded in writing.

item.title: ICE sets new Trump-era detention record in July
item.description: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement detentions reached a record high in July for President Trump's second term, internal data shows. CBS News' Camilo Montoya-Galvez has the latest.

item.title: Why the 2027 Met Gala is already causing controversy
item.description: Designer John Galliano is known for his theatrical and dramatic designs, but his legacy is also marked by antisemitic and racist comments.

item.title: Was Sylvie Cachay's death at Soho House an accident or murder?
item.description: An Oscar winner’s son is accused of killing his swimsuit designer girlfriend at a trendy NYC hotel.

item.title: Funeral held for family "wiped off the map" in Russian strike
item.description: At least two adults and four children were killed in the strike but the death toll could be higher as all the remains have not yet been formally identified.

item.title: Twin Falls In-N-Out shooting suspect identified after 3 killed, 7 wounded
item.description: The suspect, identified as 24-year-old Chad Williams, died from a self-inflicted gunshot wound, police said.

item.title: Massive wildfires in Northwest cause catastrophic damage
item.description: Dangerous wildfires are tearing through the Northwest, forcing thousands of people to evacuate. The fast-moving fires have already destroyed hundreds of homes. Kris Van Cleave reports.

item.title: Morocco blames Ceuta border surge on misleading info spread online
item.description: Morocco is blaming a massive surge of migrants​ into Ceuta on various factors, including "malicious exploitation of digital platforms" and the spread of misleading information.

item.title: Ariana Grande pulls out of musical over "endless, ongoing public scrutiny"
item.description: Ariana Grande had been due to star alongside her "Wicked" co-star Jonathan Bailey in a production of "Sunday in the Park with George" in 2027.

item.title: U.S.-Iran negotiations set to begin Monday, Trump says after calling off strikes
item.description: President Trump said negotiations with Iran are set to begin Monday after announcing Saturday night that he canceled a pending attack on Iran.

item.title: The Footprint
item.description: A woman is murdered in her home and the pivotal clue at the crime scene is a bloody footprint her killer left behind. "48 Hours" correspondent Erin Moriarty reports.

item.title: Savannah Guthrie asks for answers about mom Nancy after notes released
item.description: Savannah Guthrie said she and her family have been "in agony and despair ever since" her mother Nancy's disappearance in February.

item.title: Inside the Sentencing of the Gilgo Beach Serial Killer | Case by Case
item.description: After decades of waiting, the victims of Gilgo Beach serial killer Rex Heuermann finally faced him in a courtroom that became a space for grief, rage, and release. In this episode, we focus on the emotional heart of the sentencing — from raw statements to the quiet devastation of children who grew up without their mothers — and what it meant to finally say these words, face-to-face.
